title: improv·surprise · confetti
input: pointer (proximity blooms rails into a lion face)

v1.feedback: The lion-to-confetti-and-back cycle is a genuinely delightful surprise swerve that honors both the parent lion bloom and the 'confetti' word — the mane scatter reads as playful without breaking the contemplative register. The earth-tone confetti palette (gold, copper, rust, cream, warm ash) is well-chosen and avoids oversaturation. Two refinements: the SHAKE_DURATION of 2.2s feels slightly rushed for a piece tagged 'gentle' — stretching it to 3.5s with slower initial scatter velocities would let the eye savor the confetti moment rather than registering it as a glitch; and consider adding a very subtle size variation or rotation to the line segments during the scatter phase so the tumbling reads more as physical confetti leaves rather than uniform dashes translating through space.

v2.feedback: The lion silhouette from Gaussian field blobs is well-constructed and should read within 2 seconds — eyes, ears, mane tufts all distinct. The confetti scatter mechanic is a genuinely clever interpretation of the surprise word: mane particles burst and tumble as earth-toned confetti rather than neon scraps. Two refinements: additive blending on dense mane regions will wash toward white, erasing the gold/copper/rust distinctions — consider switching to NormalBlending with alpha or capping the accumulated brightness in the fragment shader. Second, the click-to-scatter interaction could benefit from a slow auto-return (confetti drifting back into lion form over ~8 seconds) rather than requiring a second click to reset, which would add the contemplative quality of watching order reassemble from chaos.
